newsitem.title: GERMANY: Merck sells U.S. rights to generic ulcer drug.
newsitem.headline: Merck sells U.S. rights to generic ulcer drug.

text.p: German chemicals and drugs group Merck KGaA said on Monday it had signed a contract transferring the exclusive rights for the marketing of a generic ulcers drug to Novopharm.
Merck said in a statement that its U.S. subsidiary Genpharm Inc had signed a contract to this effect with Novopharm's Granutec Inc. The deal refers to marketing in the U.S. market.
The drug concerned is a generic equivalent to Glaxo Wellcome PLC's Zantac.
The ulcer drug, the chemical term for which is ranitidine hydrochloride, has annual sales of about $1.6 billion in the United States.
Merck said in its statement that the transfer of the rights allows the U.S.'s Food and Drug Administration to consider whether Granutec's ANDA would be allowed to market the product.
The transfer would take place on August 29, 1997 or later if approval had not come by that date, Merck said.
